result: The manuscript provides background on H-ABC disease, stating it is caused by heterozygous TUBB4A mutations, particularly the p.Asp249Asn variant, and presents with hypomyelination, basal ganglia and cerebellar atrophy, dystonia, and motor deficits. TUBB4A encodes tubulin beta 4A, is highly expressed in CNS (especially cerebellum and white matter), and is localized to neurons and oligodendrocytes.
evaluation: These claims (C1, C2, C14-C31) are well-supported by citations to established literature (Simons et al., 2013; Hersheson et al., 2013; van der Knaap et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2014; etc.). The background information is appropriately referenced and represents accepted knowledge in the field.

result: Prior work on TUBB4A mutations showed that TUBB4AD249N overexpression in cell lines caused decreased myelin gene expression, fewer OL processes, shorter axons, and decreased dendritic branching. The taiep rat model (p.Ala302Thr mutation) showed microtubule accumulation in OLs and demyelination but this mutation has not been reported in humans.
evaluation: Claims C32-C34, C36-C37 are supported by citations to Curiel et al., 2017 and Duncan et al., 2017. These appropriately summarize prior work that motivated the current study and establish the rationale for developing a D249N-specific mouse model.

result: A novel CRISPR-Cas9 knock-in mouse model was generated with the p.Asp249Asn (c.745G>A) mutation in exon 4 of Tubb4a. The model has a known off-target synonymous mutation at p.Lys244Lys. Tubb4a gene expression levels are similar across WT, heterozygous, and homozygous mice in cerebellum, spinal cord, and striatum, indicating no transcriptional change from the mutation.
evaluation: Claims C3, C38-C41 are supported by methods description and Figure 1A-B data showing sequencing confirmation and qPCR expression analysis. The model generation is clearly documented, though the presence of an off-target mutation (C39) is a limitation that should be considered when interpreting results.

result: Homozygous Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice recapitulate H-ABC behavioral phenotypes including progressive motor dysfunction, tremor (starting ~P9), dystonia, ataxia, developmental delay in ambulation, wider ambulatory angle, reduced grip strength, impaired rotarod performance, weight loss, and inability to feed by P35-P40 (all with p<0.001 or p<0.05).
evaluation: Claims C4, C42-C51 are well-supported by comprehensive behavioral data in Figure 1 with appropriate statistical analyses (two-way ANOVA, n=10-14 mice). Multiple behavioral assays consistently demonstrate progressive motor deficits that parallel human H-ABC phenotypes. Statistical significance is properly reported.

result: Heterozygous Tubb4aD249N/+ mice show normal gait and motor function, with no abnormalities on rotarod testing at 9 months and 1 year, and display similar survival to WT littermates.
evaluation: Claims C52-C54 are supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B showing normal rotarod performance and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. This is an important finding showing the heterozygous mice do not recapitulate the human disease phenotype, which is discussed as a limitation.

result: Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice exhibit profound myelination deficits in corpus callosum and cerebellum starting at P14-P21 that worsen by end-stage (P35-P40), with decreased myelin proteins PLP and MBP confirmed by immunostaining and Western blot (p<0.001). Heterozygous mice show decreased myelination by 1 year of age (p<0.05).
evaluation: Claims C5, C55-C63 are strongly supported by multiple complementary methods: Eriochrome cyanine staining, immunofluorescence for PLP and MBP, and Western blotting shown in Figure 2 and supplements. The progressive nature of the defect is well-documented across timepoints with appropriate statistics (two-way ANOVA, n=3-4 mice/group).

result: Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice show a dramatic decrease in mature oligodendrocytes (ASPA+ cells) at all timepoints (p<0.001), but no apoptosis of mature OLs (CC1+/Caspase3+ cells) is detected at end-stage.
evaluation: Claims C6, C64-C65 are supported by ASPA immunostaining data in Figure 3C-D and CC1/Caspase3 co-labeling in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A. The lack of mature OL apoptosis suggests the decrease is due to other mechanisms (differentiation defects), which is appropriately discussed.

result: While total NG2+ OPC numbers remain unchanged in Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice, there is significant OPC apoptosis (NG2+/Caspase3+, p<0.01-0.001) and increased proliferation (NG2+/Ki-67+, p<0.05-0.01) at all timepoints. This suggests OPCs undergo cell death and are replaced, but defects in OPC differentiation result in fewer mature OLs.
evaluation: Claims C7, C66-C70 are supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3E-J showing stable total NG2+ numbers despite increased apoptosis and proliferation. The interpretation (C69-C70) is reasonable given the data, though the differentiation defect is inferred rather than directly demonstrated in vivo.

result: Electron microscopy reveals that Tubb4aD249N/D249N optic nerves contain mostly unmyelinated or thinly myelinated axons (~65% unmyelinated, ~30% thin myelin), with increased g-ratios (p<0.001), decreased axon caliber (p<0.05), microglia/macrophages with myelin debris, dying OLs, vacuoles, and astrogliosis. Similar defects are seen in spinal cord. Heterozygous mice show thinner myelin sheaths (~39% thin myelin) but less severe defects.
evaluation: Claims C71-C90 are comprehensively supported by detailed EM analysis in Figure 4 with quantitative g-ratio measurements, axon diameter analysis, and myelination percentage calculations (n=3 animals, 50 axons/animal). The ultrastructural characterization is rigorous and provides strong evidence for the myelination defects.

result: Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice show severe progressive loss of cerebellar granular neurons starting at P21 (p<0.001) with decreased cerebellar volume, increased neuronal apoptosis (NeuN+/Caspase3+, p<0.001), but no change in Purkinje neurons.
evaluation: Claims C8, C91-C96 are supported by Nissl staining, NeuN immunostaining, and Caspase3 co-labeling in Figure 5B-G with appropriate quantification (n=3-4 mice/group). The selective loss of granular neurons without Purkinje neuron loss is well-documented.

result: Striatal neurons (NeuN+ cells) are comparable to WT at P14 and P21 in Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice, but show significant loss at end-stage (p<0.01).
evaluation: Claims C9, C97-C98 are supported by NeuN quantification in striatum shown in Figure 5I-J. The delayed onset of striatal neuron loss compared to cerebellar neurons is appropriately noted and may relate to differential Tubb4a expression levels.

result: In vitro OPC cultures from Tubb4aD249N/+ and Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice show decreased total A2B5+ OPCs (p<0.01), decreased proliferation (A2B5+/Ki-67+, p<0.05-0.01), no change in apoptosis, fewer mature PLP+ OLs (p<0.05-0.01), and reduced proportion of mature OLs from total Olig2+ lineage cells (p<0.01).
evaluation: Claims C99-C104 are supported by in vitro OPC culture data in Figure 6A-F and Figure 6—figure supplement 1. The cell-autonomous effects on OPC proliferation and differentiation are demonstrated with appropriate replication (n=3 independent experiments). This complements the in vivo findings.

result: Cultured cortical neurons from Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice show decreased survival (p<0.01), significantly shorter axons (p<0.05), and a trend toward shorter dendritic arbors (not significant).
evaluation: Claims C10, C105-C108 are supported by neuronal culture data in Figure 6G-K with quantification of survival, axon length, and dendritic length (n=3 independent experiments). The cell-autonomous neuronal defects are demonstrated, though the dendritic phenotype is only a trend.

result: EB3 tracking in cultured neurons reveals no significant difference in average EB3 comet density, but greater variance in Tubb4aD249N/D249N neurons (p<0.05) with two distinct populations. EB3 comet run-time and run-length are significantly shorter in mutant neurons (p<0.001), but velocity is unchanged, indicating altered microtubule dynamics without affecting growth rates.
evaluation: Claims C11, C109-C114 are supported by live-cell EB3 imaging data in Figure 7 with appropriate quantification and statistical analysis (Kruskal-Wallis test, n=3 independent experiments). The interpretation that microtubule dynamics are altered without affecting growth rates is reasonable given the data showing decreased run-time/length but normal velocity.

result: The authors conclude that Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice demonstrate the complex cellular physiology of H-ABC, are the first model showing both neuronal and oligodendroglial defects, replicate behavioral and neurodegenerative features of H-ABC, and support altered microtubules as critical drivers of disease pathogenesis across diverse cell populations.
evaluation: Claims C12-C13, C115-C117 represent summary conclusions that are well-supported by the comprehensive data presented throughout the manuscript. The model demonstrates defects in oligodendrocytes (myelination, OPC differentiation), neurons (cerebellar and striatal loss, axonal defects), and microtubule dynamics, with behavioral phenotypes matching human disease. The conclusion that this is the first model showing both cell types is supported.

result: The authors state that Tubb4aD249N/D249N mice provide a key tool to explore molecular mechanisms and test therapeutic strategies for H-ABC.
evaluation: Claim C118 is a forward-looking statement about the utility of the model. While speculative about future applications, it is reasonable given the comprehensive characterization showing the model recapitulates key disease features. This represents a standard concluding statement for a model development paper.
